mappings.note: The tinai scheme is drawn from Sangam literature (LO-36) and the question turns on its tying each landscape to particular occupations and ways of life (LO-47). Not LO-32, because the item is about the ancient classification, not about India's actual landforms.

Analyses an Atharva Veda verse, i.e. an idea from an ancient Indian system of thought (LO-50), and relates it to landforms as the source of water, food and minerals, which is the goal's 'habitat ... and distribution of its features and resources'. LO-32 would cover only the landform list, not the reverence being analysed.
Uses Kalidasa's picture of the Himalayas, a named ancient literary work (LO-36), to explain how mountains enter myth, sacredness and pilgrimage (LO-50). Not LO-32: no mountain has to be located.

The mechanics of terrace farming and why the slope demands it - the landform deciding the shape of the farming occupation, which LO-47 names. Not LO-32, since the mountain is the given, not the answer.

Rivers as the lifelines of the plains, justified through irrigation, fishing and navigation (LO-47) resting on the sediment-built plain and its river (LO-32). The cultural half has no outcome of its own in this frame.

Natural and human-made hardships of mountain life - floods, avalanches, cold, unchecked tourism. This is the earth as a human habitat, the goal's own words; no outcome in the frame covers hazards or their management.
How mountains give rise to rivers and how plateaus cut gorges and waterfalls into their course - relationships among three of LO-32's named features. Not LO-27, no life is involved.
Case study identifying a plateau from its flat top, steep edge and black lava soil (LO-32), with a sub-part naming mining as the likely economic activity (LO-47).

Himalayan valley case: montane forest and snow leopard (LO-27) against trekking tourism and its sustainable management (LO-47). LO-32 is left off because the valley is the setting, not the thing to be identified.

Ganga plain case: sediment-built fertility (LO-32) with crops and irrigation-driven groundwater depletion (LO-47). Distinguished from the earlier population-count item, which was mapped to the goal because it asked only how many people live there.

Thar Desert case: hot desert with scant rainfall (LO-32), cacti and camels adapted to it (LO-27), and a herding community making a home in harsh country (CG-SST1). All three sub-parts are separately answerable, which is why this item takes three codes where most take one.
